conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Maya, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a way to check in on how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, especially over the past seven days.  

Everything we talk about stays between us unless you give permission to share, and there’s no “right” or “wrong” answer—just whatever is true for you. We’ll go through ten gentle questions; most moms finish in just a few minutes. When you’re ready, we can start with the first one.

Over the last week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?
Honestly, I can still laugh sometimes—like when my partner does something silly to make the baby smile—but it’s not as easy or as often as before. Mostly I’m just tired.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Sometimes I can laugh a little—like if the baby makes a funny face—but it doesn’t come as naturally as it used to. I have to remind myself to let go and enjoy the moment, and even then it feels kind of muted.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do find myself looking forward to little things—like taking the baby for a short walk or having my morning coffee—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it was before she was born. It feels more like going through the motions than real enjoyment.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… a couple of times this week. Yesterday the baby was fussy for hours and I kept thinking it must be something I ate or that I wasn’t soothing her right. I know, rationally, babies just cry, but the thought still popped up that I was doing it wrong.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A few times, yeah. Like, I’ll suddenly worry that her breathing sounds different or that the rash on her neck is getting worse, even when everything looks normal. I can usually talk myself down pretty quickly, but the worry still sneaks up out of nowhere.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky—just a quick rush of “what if something’s wrong?” once or twice, but it passes fast. I haven’t had that heart-pounding, can’t-breathe feeling.
Things have been getting on top of me
Some days, yeah. When she won’t nap and the laundry’s piled up, I feel like I’m drowning a little. I usually manage to get through it, but it’s stressful while it’s happening.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I’ve had trouble falling asleep a couple of nights, but it’s more because my mind keeps running through the next day’s to-do list than because I’m feeling really unhappy. Once I drift off I stay asleep fine.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel sad some of the time—maybe a couple of days this week. It’s not constant, but when I’m alone feeding her at 3 a.m. or when the house is quiet, this little wave of sadness hits. It usually lifts if I get out for a walk or text a friend, but yeah, it’s there.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried twice this week. Once was after a long cluster-feeding night when I couldn’t get her to settle—I just sat on the couch with tears rolling while she finally napped on my chest. The other time was when my mom left after visiting; I felt silly for feeling so weepy about it, but the tears just came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve felt tired and a little down, but I haven’t had any thoughts of hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression Screening Summary  
Date: [today]  
Patient: Postpartum mother, approximately [X] weeks post-delivery  

Symptoms / Behavioral Observations  
- Diminished enjoyment/pleasure (laughing, looking forward to activities) – present but partial.  
- Episodic, self-attributed guilt (“blaming myself unnecessarily”) when infant fussy.  
- Intermittent, non-persistent sadness noted several days/week; two crying episodes in past week.  
- Mild, situational anxiety/worry (infant health, “what-if” thoughts) – no frank panic attacks.  
- Occasional feeling of being overwhelmed, especially when daily tasks accumulate.  
- Sleep-onset difficulty 2 nights/week related to racing thoughts; no sustained nocturnal mood-related insomnia.  
- No anhedonia, appetite, or psychomotor changes volunteered.  
- Denies self-harm or suicidal ideation (Q10 negative).  

Pattern Consistency  
Low mood + reduced pleasure + tearfulness + self-reproach + mild anxiety → cluster raises screening concern for subsyndromal or mild-moderate postpartum depression and/or anxiety, not meeting full severity criteria at present.  

Screening Significance / Risk Factors  
✓ Persistent sadness/weeping  
✓ Loss of enjoyment (partial)  
✓ Self-blame/guilt  
✓ Overwhelm/coping strain  
✗ No suicidal ideation; no safety concern voiced  

Overall Screening Impression  
Patient endorses several core symptoms consistent with possible postpartum depressive or anxiety spectrum presentation; currently mild, situational, with intact reality testing and no safety issues. Continue monitoring; consider formal assessment (EPDS, PHQ-9, GAD-7) and follow-up within 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms escalate, functioning declines, or safety concerns emerge.
